```{r setup}
#| include: false
devtools::load_all("..", quiet = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
options(width = 110)

# all parts of the stacked INLA data, in the order of the INLA likelihoods,
# with the columns of the INLA formula (absent columns are NA)
stackedData <- function(inl, n = Inf) {
  parts <- list()
  for (r in names(inl$stacks)) for (p in names(inl$stacks[[r]])) {
    s <- utils::head(inl$stacks[[r]][[p]], n)
    s$.block <- if (p == "main") paste0(r, ": observations") else
      paste0(r, ": zero equations for ", p)
    parts[[length(parts) + 1]] <- s
  }
  cols <- unique(unlist(lapply(parts, names)))
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(parts, function(s) {
    for (cn in setdiff(cols, names(s))) s[[cn]] <- NA
    s[cols]
  }))
  out$.block <- factor(out$.block, unique(out$.block))
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}
```

# The idea {#idea}

## Joint scaled models {#jm}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column .compact width="52%"}
- several **longitudinal** markers $x_1, x_2, x_3, \dots$ and one or more
  **outcomes** $y$, each a mixed model (own fixed and random effects)
- each outcome depends on the **current value of each marker's linear
  predictor** $\eta^{(x)}$ through a coefficient $\gamma_{y,x}$
- fitted jointly with INLA, using the *copy trick*: a latent field $u$
  equals $\eta^{(x)}$ (a "zero equation") and the outcome uses
  $\gamma\,u$
- each equation chooses its **likelihood** (Gaussian, beta, binomial, Poisson, …)
  and the **prior distributions** of its hyperparameters and random effects
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{mermaid}
%%| echo: false
%%| fig-width: 5.5
%%{init: {"themeVariables": {"fontSize": "13px"}}}%%
flowchart TB
  D1[("x1: Gaussian")] --> E1["η(x1) = β + b₀ + b₁t<br/>(correlated)"]
  D2[("x2: Poisson")] --> E2["log λ = η(x2) = β + b₀ + b₁t<br/>(uncorrelated)"]
  D3[("x3: binomial")] --> E3["logit p = η(x3) = β + b₀<br/>(intercept only)"]
  E1 -- "0 = η − u" --> U1["u(x1 → y)"]
  E2 -- "0 = η − u" --> U2["u(x2 → y)"]
  E3 -- "0 = η − u" --> U3["u(x3 → y)"]
  U1 -- "γ₁ · u" --> EY["logit μ = η(y) = β + b₀ + Σₖ γₖ uₖ"]
  U2 -- "γ₂ · u" --> EY
  U3 -- "γ₃ · u" --> EY
  EY --> Y[("y: beta")]
```
:::
::::


## Fitting with INLA {#whyinla}

::: {.compact}
INLA can fit joint scaled models, but:

- is **difficult to run**: it is a separate program accessible (R interface not on CRAN)
- needs **restructured formulae**: all equations merged into one, variables renamed per equation
- needs **restructured data**: one stacked data set, response matrix
- uses **non-intuitive notation**: `f()` with `copy`, weights, `values`
- has **underdocumented specification** of likelihoods, priors, hyperparameters
- may need a **containerized environment** to be easily usable (on Macs, on shark)
- development is easier within a **devcontainer** (easy in VS Code, possible with RStudio)

Moreover, jsm:

- needs **additional equations**: one zero equation per (marker, outcome) pair
- needs **careful matching** of random-effect levels

:::

## Can it be simplified? {#simplify .scrollable .tiny}

The model in [jm] as INLA needs it — Gaussian, Poisson and binomial markers with
correlated, uncorrelated and intercept-only random effects, a beta outcome, priors on
precisions, SDs and the random-effect matrix (data not shown):

```{r jm-formula}
#| echo: false
#| class-output: r
set.seed(2)
d3 <- data.frame(id = sprintf("S%03d", rep(1:20, each = 3)), t = rep(c(0, 0.5, 1), 20))
d3$x1 <- rnorm(nrow(d3))
d3$x2 <- rpois(nrow(d3), 3)
d3$n  <- 10
d3$x3 <- rbinom(nrow(d3), d3$n, 0.4)
d3$y  <- runif(nrow(d3), 0.1, 0.9)
f3 <- collectFormulas(
  formOut  = list(y ~ t + re(1 | id, prior = halfNormalSd(1))),
  formLong = list(x1 ~ t + re(1 + t | id, prior = wishartPrec()),    # correlated
                  x2 ~ t + re(1 + t || id, prior = pcSd(1)),         # uncorrelated
                  x3 | trials(n) ~ t + (1 | id)),                    # intercept only
  familyOut  = list(y = betaFamily(phi = gammaPrec(1, 0.1))),
  familyLong = list(x1 = gaussianFamily(prec = pcSd(1)), x2 = poissonFamily(),
                    x3 = binomialFamily()))
inl3 <- buildInlaFormula(f3, prepareData(d3, d3, f3))
# one term per line
terms3 <- function(e) if (is.call(e) && identical(e[[1]], quote(`+`))) c(terms3(e[[2]]), list(e[[3]])) else list(e)
rhs <- vapply(terms3(inl3$formula[[3]]), deparse1, "", width.cutoff = 500L)
grp <- cumsum(startsWith(rhs, "f(") | c(TRUE, startsWith(rhs[-length(rhs)], "f(")))
rhs <- vapply(split(rhs, grp), paste, "", collapse = " + ")    # fixed effects on one line
cat("MX ~", paste(rhs, collapse = " +\n     "), "\n")
cat("\nfamily = ", deparse1(unname(inl3$families)), "\n", sep = "")
cf <- vapply(unname(inl3$controlFamily), deparse1, "", width.cutoff = 500L)
cat("\ncontrol.family = list(\n  ", paste(cf, collapse = ",\n  "), ")\n", sep = "")
```

## Our proposal: `jsm()` {#proposal}

The same model, written as mixed-model formulae:

```{r jsm-call}
#| eval: false
fit <- jsm(
  formOut  = list(y ~ t + re(1 | id, prior = halfNormalSd(1))),
  formLong = list(x1 ~ t + re(1 + t | id, prior = wishartPrec()),  # correlated
                  x2 ~ t + re(1 + t || id, prior = pcSd(1)),       # uncorrelated
                  x3 | trials(n) ~ t + (1 | id)),                  # intercept only
  familyOut  = list(y = betaFamily(phi = gammaPrec(1, 0.1))),
  familyLong = list(x1 = gaussianFamily(prec = pcSd(1)),
                    x2 = poissonFamily(), x3 = binomialFamily()),
  dataOut = d, dataLong = d
)
```

::: {.small}
- lme4 notation, brms-style `trials()`; families and priors as functions
- every outcome is linked to every marker automatically; `scaled(x1, ...)` only for non-default
  settings
- INLA formula, stacked data, renaming, zero equations and level matching are generated
:::

## `collectFormulas()`: responses and effects {#cf-terms .smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
| Specification | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `y ~ t + grp` | fixed effects (factors expand) |
| `log(y) ~ ...` | transformed response, named `y` |
| `k | trials(n) ~ ...` | binomial: successes of `n` trials |
| `cnt | exposure(pt) ~ ...` | counts with exposure |
| `(1 + t | id)` | correlated intercept + slope |
| `(1 + t || id)` | uncorrelated intercept, slope |
| `(1 | id)`, `(0 + t | id)` | intercept / slope only |
| `re(1 | id) + re(0 + t | id)` | two independent blocks |
| `(1 | site:id)` | nested grouping |
| `re(1 | id, prior = pcSd(u = 1))` | block with its prior (next slide) |
| `scaled(x1, ...)` | settings of the link to `x1` (outcomes) |
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r cf-terms}
p <- parseJsmFormula(
  log(x1) ~ t + grp +
    re(1 + t | id, prior = wishartPrec(df = 4)) +
    re(1 | site:id, prior = pcSd(u = 1)) +
    (0 + t || clinic),
  part = "long")
unlist(p$variables[c("response", "covariate")])
data.frame(
  term = vapply(p$re, function(b)
    deparse1(b$term), ""),
  group = vapply(p$re, `[[`, "", "group"),
  correlated = vapply(p$re, `[[`, NA,
                      "correlated"),
  prior = vapply(p$re, function(b)
    if (is.null(b$prior)) "-" else b$prior$dist, ""))
```
:::
::::

::: {.small}
Checked early: one response variable per formula, no duplicates, `scaled()` only in outcomes
and only for known markers, family inputs (`trials()` / `exposure()`) matching the family.
:::

## `collectFormulas()`: priors and hyperparameters {#cf-priors .smaller .scrollable}

| Constructor (defaults) | Prior on | Distribution | Parametrisation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gammaPrec(shape = 1, rate = 5e-5)` | precision $\tau$ | [Gamma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamma_distribution) | shape $\alpha$, **rate** $\beta$; $E\tau = \alpha/\beta$ |
| `pcSd(u, alpha = 0.01)` | SD $\sigma$ | [Exponential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exponential_distribution) ([PC prior](https://doi.org/10.1214/16-STS576)) | rate $\lambda = -\log(\alpha)/u$, i.e. $P(\sigma > u) = \alpha$ |
| `halfNormalSd(scale)` | SD $\sigma$ | [Half-normal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-normal_distribution) | Wikipedia's $\sigma$ = `scale` (SD of the unfolded normal) |
| `halfCauchySd(scale)` | SD $\sigma$ | [Cauchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cauchy_distribution), folded at 0 | location 0, scale $\gamma$ = `scale` |
| `wishartPrec(df = k + 2, scale = 1)` | precision matrix $\mathbf{Q}$ | [Wishart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wishart_distribution) | $W_k(\mathbf{V}, n)$: $n$ = `df`, $\mathbf{V}$ = `scale` ($s\,\mathbf{I}$ if scalar); $E\mathbf{Q} = n\mathbf{V}$ |

| Where | Hyperparameter arguments |
|---|---|
| random-effect block | `re(1 + t | id, prior = wishartPrec(df = 4))` (`|`, k > 1); `re(1 | id, prior = pcSd(u = 1))` (single / `||`: each effect) |
| Gaussian-type | `gaussianFamily(prec, link)`, `lognormalFamily(prec)`, `studentTFamily(prec, dof)`, `gammaFamily(prec, link)` |
| other families | `betaFamily(phi, link)`, `negBinomialFamily(size, link)`, `betaBinomialFamily(rho, link)`, `zeroInflatedPoissonFamily(type, prob)` |
| association $\gamma$ | `scaled(x1, hyper = list(beta = list(param = c(0, 1))))`: [Normal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution)(mean, **precision**) |

::: {.small}
`prec` / `phi` take the four scalar priors, `size` only `gammaPrec()`; any hyperparameter also
accepts a raw INLA list (`prec = list(initial = 4, fixed = TRUE)`). Priors are validated when
created and translated to INLA's `hyper` / `control.family`; no prior given → INLA default.
:::

## The stacked data {#stack}

```{r stack-plot}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12.5
#| fig-height: 5.6
# the simple model of the later slides (chunks data, forms, prepare, inla), built quietly
env <- new.env()
for (lbl in c("data", "forms", "prepare", "inla"))
  eval(parse(text = knitr::knit_code$get(lbl)), envir = env)
st <- stackedData(env$inl, n = 5)
# column of MX for which a row predicts (needed when the response is NA)
st$predict <- ifelse(grepl("zero equations", st$.block),
                     paste0(sub(":.*", "", st$.block), "_0eq"), sub(":.*", "", st$.block))
st <- st[c("predict", setdiff(names(st), "predict"))]
# a missing response in one y and one x1 observation (kept in the stack, predicted)
miss <- c(which(st$.block == "y: observations")[2], which(st$.block == "x1: observations")[3])
missCol <- c("y_y", "x1_x1")
for (k in 1:2) st[miss[k], missCol[k]] <- NA
role <- function(cn) {
  if (cn == "predict") "predict"
  else if (cn %in% names(env$inl$families)) "response matrix MX"
  else if (cn %in% unlist(lapply(env$inl$fixed, function(f) names(f$columns)))) "fixed effects"
  else if (grepl("TO|FROM|WEIGHT", cn)) "association"
  else "random effects"
}
cols <- setdiff(names(st), ".block")
tiles <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cols, function(cn) data.frame(
  row = seq_len(nrow(st)), block = st$.block, column = cn, role = role(cn),
  value = vapply(st[[cn]], function(v) if (is.na(v)) "" else if (is.numeric(v))
    format(signif(v, 2)) else sub("^[^|]*\\|", "", v), ""),
  present = !is.na(st[[cn]]) | (cn %in% missCol & seq_len(nrow(st)) %in% miss[cn == missCol]))))
isMiss <- !is.na(tiles$value) & tiles$value == "" & tiles$present
tiles$value[isMiss] <- "NA"
tiles$column <- factor(tiles$column, cols)
tiles$role <- factor(tiles$role, c("predict", "response matrix MX", "fixed effects", "random effects",
                                   "association"))
ggplot(tiles, aes(column, row)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = ifelse(present, as.character(block), NA)), colour = "white",
            linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = value, colour = value == "NA", fontface = ifelse(value == "NA", "bold", "plain")),
            size = 2.9, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "black", "TRUE" = "#c0392b")) +
  facet_grid(~ role, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#f2c14e", "#7fb3d5", "#a9d18e"), na.value = "grey94",
                    breaks = levels(st$.block), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "first 5 rows of each part; labels without response prefix; empty = NA (not part of the equation); NA = missing response, predicted") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1, family = "mono"),
        legend.position = "top", panel.grid = element_blank())
```

::: {.small}
One row per observation **and** one per zero equation. Each block fills only
its own response column of `MX` — that is how INLA assigns the likelihoods.
:::

## The pipeline {#pipeline}

| Function | Result |
|---|---|
| `collectFormulas()` | parsed formulae, variables, families, associations |
| `prepareData()` | one data frame per equation (rows, grouping factors, checks) |
| `buildInlaFormula()` | INLA formula, stacked data, `family`, `control.family` |
| `formatInlaFormula()` | annotated formula with its data |
| `latexEquation()` | model equations as LaTeX |
| `summarizeData()` | rows used / dropped, groups, zero equations |

Planned: a `jsm()` wrapper that runs all steps and calls INLA.

# A simple model {#simple}

## Simulated data {#sim}

200 subjects, 4 visits; marker `x1` with random intercept and slope, beta
outcome `y` driven by the marker's linear predictor.

```{r data}
set.seed(1)
n <- 200
d <- data.frame(id = sprintf("S%03d", rep(seq_len(n), each = 4)),
                t  = rep(c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5), n))
i <- as.integer(factor(d$id))
eta <- 1 + 0.5 * d$t + rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)[i] + rnorm(n, sd = 0.2)[i] * d$t
d$x1 <- eta + rnorm(nrow(d), sd = 0.2)                      # marker
mu <- plogis(-1 + 0.8 * eta)                                # gamma = 0.8
d$y <- rbeta(nrow(d), 20 * mu, 20 * (1 - mu))               # outcome, phi = 20
head(d, 4)
```

## Data at a glance {#glance}

```{r data-plot}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.2
sub <- d[d$id %in% unique(d$id)[1:40], ]                    # 40 of the 200 subjects
long <- rbind(data.frame(sub[c("id", "t")], value = sub$x1, process = "marker x1"),
              data.frame(sub[c("id", "t")], value = sub$y, process = "outcome y"))
ggplot(long, aes(t, value, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.35, colour = "#3b6ea5") + geom_point(size = 0.8, colour = "#3b6ea5") +
  facet_wrap(~ process, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) + labs(x = "time t", y = NULL)
```

## Step 1 — the model in formulae {#step1}

```{r forms}
forms <- collectFormulas(
  formOut  = list(y ~ t),                     # outcome: linked to x1 automatically
  formLong = list(x1 ~ t + (1 + t | id)),     # marker: correlated random intercept + slope
  familyOut = list(y = betaFamily())          # x1: gaussian (default)
)
forms$variables
vapply(forms$out$y$scaled, `[[`, "", "target")    # associations of y
```

::: {.small}
Every outcome is associated with every longitudinal response; `scaled(x1, ...)`
in the outcome formula is only needed for non-default parameters of that link.
:::

## Step 2 — data per equation {#step2}

```{r prepare}
dat <- prepareData(dataOut = d, dataLong = d, forms = forms)
head(dat$long$x1, 3)
head(dat$out$y, 3)
```

::: {.small}
Variables selected, incomplete rows dropped (`na.action`), grouping factors built,
row keys `.key`, responses checked against the family (beta: $0 < y < 1$).
:::

# INLA translation {#transl}

## Step 3 — the INLA formula {#step3 .scrollable}

```{r inla}
inl <- buildInlaFormula(forms, dat)
formatInlaFormula(inl, nrows = 0)
```

## What the names mean {#names}

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MX` | response matrix: one column per likelihood (`y_y`, `x1_x1`, `x1_x1_0eq`) |
| `y_1`, `y_t`, `x1_1`, `x1_t` | fixed effects (covariate columns, intercept = `1`) |
| `x1_1_id` + `copy` `x1_t_id` | correlated random intercept + slope (`iid2d`), slope weighted by `x1_t` |
| `x1_TO_y_id_t` | field $u$ of the zero equation $0 = \eta^{(x_1)} - u$, one value per `(id, t)` |
| `x1_WEIGHT` | $-1$ in zero-equation rows |
| `y_FROM_x1_id_t` | scaled copy $\gamma\,u$ in the outcome |

All names come from a configurable `namingScheme()`.

```{r families}
inl$families
```

# INLA data structure {#struct}

## Matching outcome and marker {#match .scrollable}

```{r zero-rows}
zr <- inl$stacks$x1$y
nrow(zr)                                       # unique (id, t) in the outcome data
head(zr[c("x1_x1_0eq", "x1_1", "x1_t", "x1_1_id", "x1_t_id", "x1_WEIGHT", "x1_TO_y_id_t")], 3)
head(inl$stacks$y$main[c("y_y", "y_FROM_x1_id_t")], 3)
```

::: {.small}
Zero-equation rows evaluate $\eta^{(x_1)}$ at the **outcome's** `(id, t)` values;
the outcome row points to the same label (`x1|TO|y|S001|0`) via the copy. Rows
are matched by values, not by row number — outcome visits without a marker
measurement still get a zero equation.
:::

```{r latex}
#| output: asis
cat(format(latexEquation(forms, dat), delim = "$$"))
```

# Beyond the simple model {#beyond}

## Families, inputs and priors {#rich-spec .scrollable}

```{r rich}
d$n <- 10; d$k <- rbinom(nrow(d), d$n, plogis(-0.5 + 0.6 * eta))      # successes of n trials
fR <- collectFormulas(
  formOut  = list(y ~ t + scaled(x1, hyper = list(beta = list(param = c(0, 1)))),
                  k | trials(n) ~ t + re(1 | id, prior = pcSd(u = 1))),
  formLong = list(x1 ~ t + re(1 + t | id, prior = wishartPrec(df = 4, scale = diag(c(1, 0.1))))),
  familyOut  = list(y = betaFamily(phi = gammaPrec(1, 0.1)),
                    k = binomialFamily(link = "probit")),
  familyLong = list(x1 = gaussianFamily(prec = pcSd(u = 1))))
inlR <- buildInlaFormula(fR, prepareData(d, d, fR))
str(inlR$controlFamily[c("y_y", "k_k")])
```

## … and their equations {#rich-eqs .scrollable}

```{r rich-latex}
#| output: asis
#| echo: false
cat(format(latexEquation(fR, prepareData(d, d, fR)), delim = "$$"))
```

## Supported families {#fams}

| Constructor | INLA | Hyperparameters | LHS input |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gaussianFamily()`, `studentTFamily()`, `lognormalFamily()` | `gaussian`, `t`, `lognormal` | `prec` (`dof`) | |
| `gammaFamily()`, `betaFamily()` | `gamma`, `beta` | `prec`, `phi` | |
| `poissonFamily()`, `negBinomialFamily()` | `poisson`, `nbinomial` | (`size`) | `exposure()` |
| `binomialFamily()`, `betaBinomialFamily()` | `binomial`, `betabinomial` | (`rho`) | `trials()` |
| `zeroInflatedPoissonFamily()`, `zeroInflatedNegBinomialFamily()` | `zeroinflated…0/1` | `prob` (`size`) | `exposure()` |
| `inlaFamily()` | any non-survival | any | both |

Priors: `gammaPrec()`, `pcSd()`, `halfNormalSd()`, `halfCauchySd()`,
`wishartPrec()` — or raw INLA `hyper` entries.

# Fitting (preview) {#fitting}

## Hand-assembled INLA call {#fit-call}

```{r fit}
#| echo: false
fitInla <- function(inl) {
  st <- stackedData(inl)
  resp <- names(inl$families)
  data <- c(as.list(st[setdiff(names(st), c(resp, ".block"))]), list(MX = as.matrix(st[resp])))
  INLA::inla(inl$formula, family = unname(inl$families), data = data,
             control.family = unname(inl$controlFamily))
}
fit <- suppressMessages(fitInla(inl))
est <- rbind(fit$summary.fixed[, c("mean", "sd")],
             fit$summary.hyperpar[c("Precision for the Gaussian observations[2]",
                                    "precision parameter for the beta observations",
                                    "Beta for y_FROM_x1_id_t"), c("mean", "sd")])
rownames(est) <- c("y: intercept", "y: t", "x1: intercept", "x1: t",
                   "x1: residual precision", "y: beta precision phi", "gamma (x1 -> y)")
est$true <- c(-1, 0, 1, 0.5, 25, 20, 0.8)
knitr::kable(round(est[c("true", "mean", "sd")], 2))
```

::: {.small}
`inla(inl$formula, family = inl$families, control.family = inl$controlFamily, data = <stacked data>)`
recovers the simulated values (200 subjects). The `jsm()` wrapper will do this assembly.
:::

## Development container {#devcont}

:::: {.columns}

- image based on `rocker/geospatial` (R 4.5) with **INLA**, `lme4`, `devtools`,
  Quarto
- VS Code: *Dev Containers: Reopen in Container*; the repository is mounted at
  `/home/rstudio/project`
- VS Code extensions: R, Quarto, Live Server, Claude Code
- **RStudio Server** on port 8787

```sh
git clone -b devel-ai \

code mvrem   # -> Reopen in Container
```

## Non-AI vs AI development {#nonai-vs-ai .smaller}

- 1st implementation (human-written, GitHub Copilot):
  - INLA formula and data were generated
  - no lme4 input (lack of proper specification)
- 2nd implementation (human-written, GitHub Copilot):
  - working, limited support for complex model specifications and priors
- 3rd implementation (Claude Code written):
  - **no single line of R code** written manually
  - problem approached in small steps with prior (?deep?) understanding
  - auto-generated code, documentation, **tests**
  - iterative refinement based on **auto-testing** and human feedback
  - no hallucinations observed (all code and documentation are grounded in the task)
  - broader support for complex model specifications, priors, latex
  - some deeper coding mistakes (which I made in the 2nd implementation and I did not properly describe), were also made by Claude Code
